stubs.service: Remote participant (the other person in the P2P room)
stubs.how: ZestSend has no accounts or stored history: chat, files, the shared document and the canvas exist only between two connected peers. start.sh runs .ui-capture/peer/dist/bot.mjs, which runs the app's own client modules (NativeWebRTCSession, FileTransferManager, P2PCollaborationProvider from src/client/lib) in Node with @roamhq/wrtc as RTCPeerConnection. It joins room 2468 through the app's real signaling Durable Object and connects to the browser over a real WebRTC data-channel connection on localhost. Every time a browser joins, it replays its side of the session: 31 chat messages, 9 file offers (files can actually be accepted and downloaded), and a Yjs document and canvas that sync into the Document and Canvas tabs.

stubs.service: Cloudflare Realtime TURN API (/api/turn/credentials -> rtc.live.cloudflare.com generate-ice-servers) and the TURN relay itself
stubs.how: start.sh sets placeholder TURN_ID/TURN_TOKEN and writes them into dist/zestsend/.dev.vars together with TURN_API_ORIGIN=http://127.0.0.1:$PORT/__stubs/turn. src/worker/index.ts reads TURN_API_ORIGIN, falling back to the real Cloudflare origin. The front server answers POST /__stubs/turn/v1/turn/keys/:id/credentials/generate-ice-servers like the real API: it checks the bearer token, then returns {iceServers:[stun, turn + username/credential]} with fresh per-request credentials. Those credentials are registered on a real local STUN/TURN server (node-turn, UDP 127.0.0.1 on a port picked free at startup) run by the same process. So /api/turn/credentials returns 200 and the TURN probe gets real relay candidates.

stubs.service: Public STUN servers (stun.l.google.com etc., hardcoded in webrtc.ts)
stubs.how: Not stubbed. With no network the STUN probes time out after about 4.5s and the connection diagnostics show STUN as unavailable. The P2P connection still forms over localhost host candidates (route: direct).

app.notes: Setup: mise.toml pins node 22.23.5 and pnpm 11.1.3 (GitHub attestation checks turned off because api.github.com/sigstore are unreachable from the sandbox). .ui-capture/build.sh runs pnpm install, then `pnpm build` (tsc + vite with @cloudflare/vite-plugin) with VITE_INSIGHTFLARE_ORIGIN pointed at the stub, then installs and bundles the peer bot (esbuild). lib0 is installed from a repack of the same 0.2.117 tarball without its .vscode/ folder (pnpm override in pnpm-workspace.yaml), because the sandbox cannot write .vscode paths. start.sh wipes .wrangler/state (ephemeral room seats) and picks free internal ports. It runs `vite preview` (the built Worker + Room Durable Object in local workerd/miniflare) on an internal port, and the front server .ui-capture/stub-server.mjs on $PORT (4442). The front server answers the stubs under /__stubs/ and proxies everything else, WebSocket signaling included, to the app. start.sh waits until the page, the analytics stub and /api/turn/credentials all answer successfully, then starts the peer bot in room 2468. If any process exits, start.sh exits non-zero. Open http://localhost:4442/en/room/2468. The browser joins as the second participant; after about 5s (offline STUN probes time out) the connection dialog closes and the room shows a live session with 'Mira', a designer working with the viewer on the 'Harbor Line 2.3' ferry-app release. Data: Chat has 31 incoming messages, short and long, with emoji, code-ish strings, a self-correction and a brb/back. Files has 9 incoming offers (hero PNG, contract .docx, release-notes PDF, a 24.6MB screenshot zip, a standup .m4a, an invoice .xlsx, brand-tokens.json, a 58MB onboarding .mp4, a .HEIC photo); accept any of them to see a real transfer. The Document tab has a launch checklist with headings, a task list with checked and unchecked items, bullets, a blockquote, a JSON code block and links. The Canvas tab has an onboarding-flow wireframe sketch (3 phone screens, swipe arrows, a red annotation circle, plus a few strokes by the viewer, one of them erased). Other main areas: the home page /en with a 4-digit room code entry, voice/video calls and screen share (need camera/mic permission), shared playback, connection diagnostics. Since the UI stores no history, messages show as 'just now' and only the peer's side of the chat exists until the viewer types something. Reload the page (or open it again) and the bot replays the session. I could not take screenshots myself: the sandbox kills headless Chromium. Verification used a Node stand-in client (.ui-capture/peer/probe.ts), which received all chats, offers, document, strokes and file bytes.
